trigger: Operator: 'Choose detected API ... search all combinations ... We MUST receive results from API! However, in reality we never get any results, search does not work and we cannot use the apps!'
method: systematic-debugging Phase 1 (reproduce + gather evidence at each boundary) on the LIVE containerized KVM emulator + running goapi. NO fix before root cause. All findings backed by captured evidence.

findings.statement: The API layer RETURNS REAL RESULTS. Direct goapi :8443 curl (Lava-Auth derived from .env): archiveorg×story HTTP200 50 results (totalPages 16939); thepiratebay×linux 200 results; torrentscsv×1080p 50 results; gutenberg×linux real result. gutenberg×1080p + yts×1080p legitimately 0 (query/catalogue mismatch — expected). The prior-session VPN-egress issue is RESOLVED on this host.
findings.implication: operator's 'no results' is NOT an API-layer bug.

findings.statement: The CLIENT → HOST-GOAPI search path WORKS end-to-end on the device. autonomous-qa run-matrix --backend goapi --subsets archiveorg --queries story: verdict=PASS, tests=1 fail=0, marker_download_ok=true. onboard→search→results→download all succeeded. Evidence: .lava-ci-evidence/autonomous-qa/2026-07-04/goapi/archiveorg-story/verdict.json
findings.implication: the client search UI, request-building, response-parsing (SearchResultDto, ignoreUnknownKeys+lenient), and rendering are CORRECT when pointed at a reachable API. All 12 providers declare SEARCH capability.

findings.statement: The on-device api-app embed CRASHES on startup on the x86_64 emulator. Controlled repro (install api-app debug, am start --ez lava.applink.START_API true), FULL logcat captured. Tombstone: 'Fatal signal 31 (SIGSYS), code 1 (SYS_SECCOMP)', 'Cause: seccomp prevented call to disallowed x86_64 system call 6' (rax=6 = lstat), 'backtrace: #00 liblavaapi.so (internal/runtime/syscall/linux.Syscall6+14) BuildId 30b543eb...', 'Process 4186 exited due to signal 31 (Bad system call)' ~3s after launch, thread name 'DefaultDispatch' (Go scheduler). ABI x86_64, Android 14 emulator.
findings.root_cause: The embedded Go .so (liblavaapi.so, GOOS=android GOARCH=amd64, Go 1.26) calls raw x86_64 syscall 6 (lstat) at startup (Go file-op path — TLS cert / SQLite dir), which Android's x86_64 app-seccomp allowlist BLOCKS. On arm64 (real devices) there is no lstat syscall (Go uses fstatat) so it does NOT crash there — this is x86_64-emulator-specific. Our lava-api-go code has NO direct os.Lstat/filepath.Walk; the lstat originates in the Go stdlib/runtime file-op path on android/amd64.
findings.so_health_probe: /health never passes (embed process dead) — confirmed FAIL after 33×3s.
findings.fix_direction: OWED (deep): make the embed avoid raw lstat on android/amd64 — options: (a) a Go build workaround / runtime patch so os file ops use fstatat on android/amd64; (b) eliminate/deferred the startup file-stat; (c) upstream Go issue. Requires focused Go-embed work; NOT a one-line change.

findings.severity: MISDIAGNOSIS — guest actually HAS validated WAN (2026-07-04 correction)
findings.original_statement: The containerized KVM emulator has NO guest WAN/DNS: `adb shell ping -c1 8.8.8.8` = WAN-IP-FAIL, `ping gutenberg.org` = DNS-FAIL.
findings.correction: The ping-based 'no WAN' conclusion was an ICMP false-negative. qemu user-mode networking (slirp) and rootless podman both DROP raw ICMP but FORWARD TCP/UDP. Definitive live re-test on the same running emulator: (a) guest `toybox nc www.gutenberg.org 80` returned `HTTP/1.1 302 Found` — a real internet response from INSIDE the Android guest; (b) `dumpsys connectivity` shows the active default network (100, WIFI) as `IS_VALIDATED&EVER_VALIDATED` with `Capabilities: INTERNET&VALIDATED`, `firstValidated`/`lastValidated` timestamps, DNS 10.0.2.3-6, default route via 10.0.2.2 — Android's own captive-portal/internet validation probe (which requires reaching the WAN) PASSED; (c) the podman container itself has TCP WAN (`curl https://www.gutenberg.org/ -> 200`, `https://rutracker.org/ -> 301`). The guest→slirp→container→internet TCP path is fully working.
findings.implication: With F3 fixed, the on-device api-app embed CAN reach providers over the WAN. No emulator-WAN work is owed. The manual-curl HTTP 401 seen while testing was the embed's ContentProvider-gated API key (the real client reads it via the same-signature `apiKeyAuthority` provider during onboarding), NOT a WAN failure.
findings.fix_direction: NONE — non-issue. The full end-to-end api-app search proof runs via the autonomous-qa harness (--backend apiapp), which performs real onboarding (client obtains the embed key) then search.

operator_scenario_conclusion: RESOLVED 2026-07-04. The operator's 'search returns no results / cannot use the apps' on the api-app ('detected API') path was caused by F3 (embed SIGSYS/lstat crash on x86_64 from modernc/libc's musl fast-path legacy syscalls). F3 is FIXED (libc-fork dispatcher remap → *at; live gate: SIGSYS=0, /health 200, mDNS advertised). F4 ('no WAN') was a MISDIAGNOSIS (ICMP-only false-negative; guest has validated TCP WAN). With F3 fixed, the on-device embed serves REAL search results over the guest WAN: archiveorg×story HTTP200 ~50 results, archiveorg×linux ~50, torrentscsv×1080p ~25, gutenberg×linux ~1 (real catalogue match) — proof at F3-fix-evidence/2026-07-04-EMBED-SEARCH-WORKS-PROOF.md + the saved result JSONs. The client authenticates to the embed via the Lava-Auth header (base64(16 random bytes) per-install key, ApiKeyStore); Auth-Token is the separate provider-cookie header.
f5_test_automation_note: A SEPARATE test-automation limitation (F5, NOT a product bug): the autonomous-qa Challenge70 apiapp path launches the sibling api-app whose 'Back to Lava client' Compose button cannot be reliably clicked by UiAutomator (client-bound ComposeTestRule cannot reach the cross-process Compose surface; coordinate/accessibility clicks on the button did not register). The PRODUCT works (proven by the direct embed-search evidence above + the real client uses the identical Lava-Auth auth path); the automated end-to-end Challenge for the apiapp backend is being hardened separately. The goapi backend Challenge is green (F2).
